issues.reason: The relative clause is irrealis "would have V-ed" content, and *Counterfactual conditionals* is explicit that a would-have consequent is sealed and "not asserted either way", so emitting it as a positive top-level event bundle asserts a legalizing the sentence marks as unrealized (*Core patterns*: assert only what the text states).

The half that stands is the diagnosis that nothing marks the legalizing as unrealized; the half that does not is the implied remedy — no licensed irrealis carrier exists for a bare "would have" relative clause (Counterfactual needs an if-antecedent the text lacks), so the fix is removal, not a status atom.

"Legalize" is a deadjectival causative that makes its object legal — a change of the object's own state in the same non-physical sense the instruction set grants cancel/postpone and compile/redact — so Patient is licensed and the "when the test is unclear, default to Theme" clause does not fire.

gaps_confirmed: Irrealis "would have V-ed" in a relative clause with no if-antecedent: Counterfactual is defined only for the subjunctive if/would-have pair, so there is no licensed non-asserting encoding for it.
No event-level extent slot: clause adverbs of extent or margin ("fully" legalized, "narrowly" defeated) can only land in Manner, which records how the action was done rather than how much.
repair_summary: Removed the eight atoms realizing the unasserted relative clause — the legalize event class, its Agent/Patient/Manner/For/Location atoms, and the medical_purpose genus and modifier atoms that only that clause introduced; kept the projected proper-name atom for Connecticut and left the matrix defeat clause byte-identical.
notes: The matrix clause (agentless passive defeat, Past, Manner, Location, Weekday) was never in dispute and is untouched. With no licensed carrier for "would have", the bill's content is now unrecorded — that is the confirmed gap, not a further defect.
